title: CLAUDE.md
text: Use UK English spelling throughout (e.g. “serialise”, “centralise”, “behaviour”, “colour”, “summarise”) Follow existing code style: snake_case functions variables Use cli error handling (codeminer_abort, codeminer_warn, codeminer_inform) Use glue::glue_sql() parameterised SQL queries Use dplyr / dbplyr lazy table operations possible Prefer tidyverse packages already Imports (dplyr, purrr, stringr, tidyr, tibble) base R equivalents read clearly — e.g. purrr::map() rather loop rows, stringr::str_sub() rather substr(). title: Introduction to codeminer
text: multiple versions lookup, mapping, relationship table available, codeminer resolves "latest" automatically. first time query function resolves "latest" given code type, resolved version cached remainder session. avoids repeated informational messages ensures consistent version usage across workflow. can override current session codeminer_set_version(): Pins affect default "latest" resolution. Explicit version arguments always take precedence: clear version selections return automatic "latest" resolution: can also clear versions selectively code type: codeminer_status() shows active versions alongside connection info.
code: # Pin lookup and relationship versions for a code type codeminer_set_version(   lookup       = c("ICD-10" = "UKB v4"),   relationship = c("ICD-10" = "UKB v4") )  # Pin a mapping version (use "from > to" format for the key) codeminer_set_version(   mapping = c("Read v3 > ICD-10" = "UKB v4") ) # This uses the pinned version for ICD-10: CODES("E10", type = "ICD-10") #> <codeminer_codelist>: 1 code #> Code type: "ICD-10" #>  #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   code  description              code_type #>   <chr> <chr>                    <chr>     #> 1 E10   Type 1 diabetes mellitus ICD-10  # This ignores the pin and uses "UKB v4" directly: CODES("E10", type = "ICD-10", lookup_version = "UKB v4") #> <codeminer_codelist>: 1 code #> Code type: "ICD-10" #>  #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   code  description              code_type #>   <chr> <chr>                    <chr>     #> 1 E10   Type 1 diabetes mellitus ICD-10 codeminer_clear_versions() # Clear only the ICD-10 lookup version codeminer_clear_versions(lookup = "ICD-10")  # Clear lookup and relationship for SNOMED CT codeminer_clear_versions(   lookup = "SNOMED CT",   relationship = "SNOMED CT" )

title: Column filters
text: Filters declared table metadata, per column, values (valid options) defaults (applied nothing overrides ). column may also carry two optional documentation fields, filters self-describing: description: single string explaining column means. value_labels: named character vector mapping values human-readable labels (names must subset values; labelling may partial). defaults value set applied default. include every value default, list — column unrestricted default still available narrow. exclude everything default, use empty defaults (rarely wanted). rest vignette uses small lookup registered dummy database. status filtered active codes default; module lists values defaults, modules included default: Filters existing table can changed without re-adding data via update_lookup_metadata() (mapping/relationship equivalents).

title: Column filters
text: Every query function accepts col_filters: "default" (default): session pins set, else metadata defaults. NULL (NA): filtering table query touches. table-keyed list (): entry replaces table’s pinned/default filters wholesale; unnamed tables keep pins/defaults. NA table entry un-filters one table. entry replaces whole set, “tweak one column, keep rest” done data space: take current filters, amend, pass back (see round-trip workflow). Typos don’t fail silently: entry matches registered table, column absent table, value outside column’s registered values trigger warning naming available.

text: code_type type coding system (e.g., ICD-10, SNOMED-CT) relationship_version version relationship metadata (default: "v0") ... dots future extensions must empty. from_col column name source code relationship (default: "") to_col column name target code relationship (default: "") type_col column name relationship type, NA (default) relationship table purely hierarchical (every edge child-parent, type column type filtering). child_parent_relationship_code value type_col indicates child-parent (-) relationship, NA (default) purely hierarchical table. Must NA type_col NA. relationship_source source relationship metadata (default: NA_character_) col_filters Optional column filter specification. named list element list values (valid values) defaults (default filter values), plus optional description (single string) value_labels (named character vector, names subset values) documentation fields. See lookup_metadata() full format. NULL (default) means column filters.
